bridges.boundary: Some forms of digital access require reliable power, but power is not a complete model of Internet use.
General connectivity and educational use differ; no causal learning improvement is established.
Possible digital-health access intersection, but digital access does not substitute for personnel or primary care.
Hydrological observations may inform adaptation planning, not prove improved harvests.
Groundwater observation connects to depletion questions without showing management efficacy.
Food access can relate to nutrition/health risks; these sources do not establish causal NCD effects.
Household housing costs and medical expenditures can compete for income, without local effect estimates.
Grid constraints can affect electricity quality, but many local access deficits have other mechanisms.
Water and access to health systems may share vulnerable populations; there is no direct estimated relationship here.
Reliable power may be an input to cold chains, but no specific post-harvest effect is quantified here.
Affordability and homelessness overlap but should not be conflated or given a causal coefficient.
Building efficiency may affect energy demand and affordability, but not directly verified here.
Privacy-enhancing technologies may address selected threats without end-to-end guarantees.
Population observation may inform dog-mediated rabies control, but infection outcomes are not evaluated.
Meaningful connectivity for learning is a proposed prerequisite not an outcome-equivalent.
Affordability and resilience are overlapping housing dimensions but not the same measured outcome.
